title: E-Wrap Cast On
transcriptHtml:
E-Wrap Cast On

What the E-Wrap Cast On Is

The e-wrap cast on is similar to the hand knitting thumb cast on. It’s quick and easy, and it makes a neat edge with a lot of stretch.

Wrapping the Needles

Simply wrap each needle with a single strand of yarn in a counterclockwise direction. Think of the script letter e as you wrap.

Preparing to Knit the First Row

To make the first row easier to knit, keep the stitches pushed back toward the bed of the machine. This helps the needles knit more smoothly.

Weights, Waste Yarn, and Ravel Cord

When you’re done wrapping, you’ll have loops on each needle, but you can’t easily hang weights. Using a cast on comb eliminates this problem, but a cast on comb isn’t always available.

It’s suggested that you cast on with waste yarn and ravel cord. First hang weights, and then e-wrap each needle.

Removing the Work

After you remove the work from the machine, you can easily remove the ravel cord and the waste knitting. This technique can be used on any machine, and it creates a beautiful e-wrap cast on.

Keywords: e-wrap cast on, thumb cast on, machine knitting cast on, counterclockwise wrap, first row knitting, cast on comb, waste yarn and ravel cord, stretchy cast on edge
